rules.title: Alabama — Minors 14-15: 30-min break after 5 continuous hours

result.summary: Minors 14 and 15 may not work more than 5 continuous hours without a 30-minute break (Child Labor Law; rate in force by 2000).

rules.title: Alaska — Minors under 18: 30-min break on shifts of 6+ hours

result.summary: A minor scheduled for 6 or more consecutive hours gets a 30-minute break after the first 1.5 hours and before the last hour; a minor who has worked 5 consecutive hours without a break gets one before continuing. Modifiable by CBA or occasional mutual agreement.

rules.title: Delaware — Minors under 18: 30-min break after 5 consecutive hours

result.summary: Minors under 18 may not work more than 5 consecutive hours without a non-work period of at least 30 minutes.

rules.title: Florida — Minors 15 and under: 30-min break per 4 continuous hours

result.summary: Minors 15 and younger may not work more than 4 continuous hours without a 30-minute uninterrupted break.

rules.title: Florida — Minors 16-17 working 8+ hours: 30-min break per 4 continuous hours

result.summary: From 2024-07-01 (HB 49, ch. 2024-25) 16- and 17-year-olds who work 8 or more hours in a day may not work more than 4 continuous hours without a 30-minute break; shorter days have no state break requirement. Home-education and virtual-school students are exempt.

citations.source: Fla. Stat. §450.081(4) as amended by ch. 2024-25

rules.title: Hawaii — Minors 14-15: 30-min break after 5 continuous hours

result.summary: Minors 14 and 15 may not work more than 5 hours continuously without a rest or lunch interval of at least 30 consecutive minutes.

rules.title: Illinois — Minors under 16: 30-min meal period by the 5th consecutive hour

result.summary: Minors under 16 who work more than 5 continuous hours get a meal period of at least 30 minutes starting no later than the fifth hour (Child Labor Law of 2024, effective 2025-01-01, carrying forward 820 ILCS 205/4).

rules.title: Indiana — Minors under 18: breaks totaling 30 min on shifts of 6+ hours

result.summary: A minor scheduled to work 6 or more consecutive hours gets one or two breaks totaling at least 30 minutes.

rules.title: Iowa — Minors under 16: 30-min break on shifts of 5+ hours

result.summary: A person under 16 employed 5 hours or more gets an intermission of at least 30 minutes.

rules.title: Kentucky — Minors under 18: 30-min lunch by the 5th hour

result.summary: Minors under 18 get a lunch period of at least 30 minutes no later than the fifth hour of work (not within the first 3 hours).

rules.title: Louisiana — Minors under 16: 30-min meal after 5 hours

result.summary: Minors under 16 who work 5 hours get a meal period of at least 30 minutes.

rules.title: Maryland — Minors under 18: 30-min break per 5 consecutive hours

result.summary: A minor may not work more than 5 consecutive hours without a non-working period of at least 30 minutes.

rules.title: Michigan — Minors under 18: 30-min break per 5 continuous hours

result.summary: A minor may not work more than 5 continuous hours without a documented 30-minute meal and rest period.

rules.title: New Jersey — Minors under 18: 30-min break after 5 continuous hours

result.summary: A minor under 18 may not work more than 5 hours continuously without an interval of at least 30 minutes.

rules.title: North Carolina — Minors under 16: 30-min break after 5 consecutive hours

result.summary: Youths under 16 get a 30-minute break after any period of 5 consecutive hours of work.

rules.title: Ohio — Minors under 18: 30-min rest period per 5 consecutive hours

result.summary: No minor may work more than 5 consecutive hours without a rest period of at least 30 minutes.

rules.title: Oklahoma — Minors under 16: 30-min rest after 5 consecutive hours

result.summary: Minors under 16 may not work more than 5 consecutive hours without a 30-minute rest period.

rules.title: Oklahoma — Minors under 16: one cumulative hour of rest on 8-hour days

result.summary: Minors under 16 working 8 consecutive hours get one cumulative hour of rest periods (in addition to the 30-minute break rule).

rules.title: Oregon — Minors under 18: 30-min meal on shifts of 6+ hours

result.summary: Minors get a 30-minute duty-free meal period for each work period of 6 or more hours (no waiver, no on-duty meal).

rules.title: Oregon — Minors under 18: paid 15-min rest per 4 hours

result.summary: Minors get a paid 15-minute rest period for every 4-hour segment (or major part) worked, separate from the meal period.

rules.title: Pennsylvania — Minors under 18: 30-min meal per 5 consecutive hours

result.summary: A minor may not work more than 5 consecutive hours without a 30-minute meal period (Child Labor Act, Act 151 of 2012, effective 2013-01-22).

rules.title: Tennessee — Minors under 18: 30-min break on shifts of 6+ hours

result.summary: A minor scheduled to work 6 consecutive hours gets a 30-minute unpaid break or meal period, not during or before the first hour; the adult waiver and ample-opportunity exceptions do not apply.

rules.title: Utah — Minors under 18: 30-min meal by the 5th hour

result.summary: Minors get a meal period of at least 30 minutes not later than 5 hours after the workday begins; paid if the minor cannot be fully relieved of duty.

rules.title: Utah — Minors under 18: paid 10-min rest per 4 hours

result.summary: Minors get a paid rest period of at least 10 minutes for every 4 hours (or fraction) worked and may not work more than 3 consecutive hours without one.

rules.title: Virginia — Minors under 16: 30-min break after 5 hours

result.summary: Children under 16 may not work more than 5 hours continuously without a lunch period of at least 30 minutes.

rules.title: Washington — Minors 14-15: 30-min meal within 4 hours

result.summary: Minors under 16 get an uninterrupted 30-minute meal period beginning before the fourth consecutive hour of work; may not be waived.

rules.title: Washington — Minors 14-15: paid 10-min rest per 2 hours

result.summary: Minors under 16 get a paid 10-minute rest break within every 2 consecutive hours of work, in addition to meal periods.

rules.title: Washington — Minors 16-17: 30-min meal within 5 hours

result.summary: 16- and 17-year-olds get an uninterrupted 30-minute meal period beginning before the fifth consecutive hour of work; may not be waived.

rules.title: Washington — Minors 16-17: paid 10-min rest per 4 hours

result.summary: 16- and 17-year-olds get a paid 10-minute rest break for every 4 hours worked and may not work more than 3 hours without one.

rules.title: Wisconsin — Minors under 18: 30-min meal on shifts over 6 hours

result.summary: Minors may not work more than 6 consecutive hours without a duty-free meal period of at least 30 minutes.
